subject: SpireCheck — spike in latency + error rate (customer-facing rollback plan)
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@spirecheck.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Narang <priya.narang@spirecheck.com>, SpireCheck Oncall <oncall@spirecheck.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate & 95th% latency spike — impacting checkout

Hannah / David —

We started seeing a spike in failed model calls and a big jump in 95th percentile latency around 08:45 PDT. The checkout path is intermittently returning 500s and timing out for some users. Our engineering team is seeing elevated retry rates and queues backing up in our service.

I attached a short snapshot of the customer-visible errors and a few traces. Can you confirm whether there was any model rollout or config change on your side? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is impacting our conversion funnel.

Attachments: error_snapshot_20270523.log, response-traces-20270523.json

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Platform Engineering
SpireCheck
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@spirecheck.com>, Priya Narang <priya.narang@spirecheck.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate & 95th% latency spike — impacting checkout

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We are standing up a priority bridge now.

Immediate plan (next 45 mins):
- Internal triage (engineering + infra + oncall) to identify whether this is serving-side degradation or a model variant issue.
- If the spike correlates with a recent model/quantization change, prepare immediate rollback to prior variant.
- Temporary routing/fallback: enable the reserve model pool for your tenant to reduce tail latency.

David is leading the triage. Marissa will coordinate customer comms and confirm the SLA remediation timeline. Karthik — please confirm whether we can trigger an emergency canary rollback and expected impact to throughput.

I will keep you updated every 30 minutes with an executive-friendly summary. We can also escalate to the C-suite if we need quota/priority capacity beyond reserved.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability (EMEA & US)
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@spirecheck.com>, Priya Narang <priya.narang@spirecheck.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate & 95th% latency spike — triage notes

Quick triage update — initial telemetry from the serving nodes:

- Around 08:43 PDT we saw a coordinated increase in requests with longer sequence lengths (customer-side burst) plus a simultaneous async cache invalidation from a downstream cache refresh.
- Error type: elevated 500-level responses are predominantly OOM-rejections on quantized model pipelines (nvll/quant-8 path).
- Throughput: token-per-second processing on affected GPU pool dropped ~30% at the peak, queue length doubled.

Probable contributing factors: traffic shape change + a recent quantization kernel fallback that increased memory pressure under certain sequence patterns. No infra instance restarts or deployments in the same window.

Immediate mitigations we can execute (need go-ahead):
1) Roll back the quantized variant for SpireCheck to the previous float16 variant (estimated 6–9 min to complete; will reduce tail errors but increase per-token cost ~10%).
2) Temporarily enable per-tenant reserve pool routing — moves traffic to isolated capacity with lower contention (estimated 3–5 min to apply, requires authorization for priority usage).
3) Apply short-term request shaping on SpireCheck endpoints (drop/queue very large sequences) — customer-visible but buys time.

I recommend (1) + (2) in parallel. If you approve, I will kick off the rollback and notify infra to provision reserve capacity.

Attachments: rollback-play.pdf (internal rollback checklist)

—David
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@spirecheck.com>, Priya Narang <priya.narang@spirecheck.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate & 95th% latency spike — rollback authorization

Hannah / David —
We can execute the rollback and the temporary reserve routing now. Two notes:
- Rollback impact: model latency per-token will be slightly higher, but tail errors should drop to baseline; we will mark this as an emergency canary rollback (no major customer-facing model change besides improved reliability).
- Capacity/credits: switching SpireCheck onto reserve capacity will burn into their reserved burst allowance; if they exceed it we will need approval to move to prioritized billing for the window. Marissa — please coordinate the customer authorization and offer a credit if needed.

Give me the green light and I will trigger the rollback; estimated rollback completion by 10:37 PDT and reserve routing by 10:40 PDT.

—Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@spirecheck.com>, Priya Narang <priya.narang@spirecheck.com>

Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate & 95th% latency spike — customer-facing summary and next steps

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for working with us on this. Short summary and ask: we will perform an emergency rollback of the quantized model variant for your tenant and route your traffic to an isolated reserve pool to cut the tail errors. Expected timeline: rollback complete and routing in place by ~10:45 PDT; we will monitor and report back at 11:15 and 12:00 with progress.

What we need from you:
- Please confirm that you approve the rollback + temporary reserve routing.
- If you prefer not to route to reserve capacity (billing impact), we can instead apply request shaping as a softer mitigation — please advise.

We will provide an executive summary to your leadership at 13:00 PDT and a full post-incident write-up within 48 hours. We will also proactively suggest a tuning profile to avoid similar memory-pressure patterns.

Customer-visible impact: expected reduction in 500s and tail latency; slight increase in average per-request CPU/GPU cost for the window.

Attachments: rollback-play.pdf (internal), incident-ack-template.txt

—Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Escalations Lead
Redwood Inference
